speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether he can provide an update on the recognition of health passports issued by the International Air Transport Association and individual countries; and (b) how can the Singapore Government verify the authenticity of the Immunity Health Passport issued by the respective countries with regard to personal immunisation records and COVID-19 test results.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: We understand that we are now negotiating travel corridors, rather than travel bubbles.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: And one of the important factors hinges on the vaccine passport.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: We are glad that we have started discussions.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: But having said that, some countries in Asia, especially one country in North Asia, had experienced a vaccination scam, even a Member of Parliament was also a victim of this vaccination scam.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Different countries have different ways of identifying residents who have gone for the vaccination and what type of vaccination.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: So, my supplementary question to the Senior Minister of State is that, first, what are the type of vaccinations that we will recognise in the vaccination passport?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The first step is how do we establish ways to verify the authenticity of these certificates?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, in other words, I need to make sure that when you say that you are tested and it is PCR negative, or when you say that you are vaccinated, I can trust that this information is accurate and there is a way to do this.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I think that is the first step: establishing the checks to verify how authentic, how accurate is this information.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The second step is, once you have this information, then what do you do with it.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because it really depends on, first of all, what is the rate of infection in that source country, how confident are we of the risk level of this individual, when he or she travels to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And that would then determine what kind of safeguards we put in place.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I think to answer Mr Ang's questions, this is an ongoing discussion with the countries that I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But we should view this, really, as a two-stage process.
